pass_a_gloss: Pillars of the Church, such as Peter and John, who [have] as foundation Christ, called gold. Marble, those whom Paul called ground/bulwark; on account of the steady and unshaken, and by the bright life and the sound word the common body of the Church bearing and supporting. But also the loving God from whole heart, and the neighbor as oneself, as through marble pillars, [is] to bear the common body of the Church. For the one perfected in these two commandments is made pillar and ground of the Church; so that by these two right deeds the whole body of the Church, as on certain legs, is supported, the golden foundation of the base according to faith producing the unbending and unchangeable and the in-every-good firm in the thoughts.
pass_b_english: The pillars of the Church are men such as Peter and John (Galatians 2:9), who have Christ as their foundation (1 Corinthians 3:11), and He is the one here called gold. They are marble, the men Paul called a bulwark (1 Timothy 3:15), because they are steady and unshaken, and by their shining life and sound speech they bear up and support the common body of the Church.

Moreover, to love God with all one's heart, and one's neighbor as oneself (Matthew 22:37–39), is to bear the common body of the Church as on pillars of marble. For whoever has been made perfect in these two commandments (Matthew 22:40) is made a pillar and bulwark of the Church. So the whole body of the Church rests on these two achievements as if on legs, while the golden foundation, the base of faith, sets in their thoughts a steadiness that does not bend or shift and stands firm in every good.
source_text:
μαρμαρίνους τεθεμελιωμένους ἐπὶ βάσεις χρυσᾶς. Στύλοι δὲ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, οἷον
Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάννης, οἳ θεμέλιον τὸν Χριστὸν χρυσὸν λεχθέντα. Μαρμάρινοι δὲ,
οὕσπερ εἶπε Παῦλος ἑδραίωμα· διὰ τὸ ἑδραῖον καὶ ἀσάλευτον, καὶ τῷ λαμπρῷ βίῳ
καὶ τῷ ὑγιαίνοντι λόγῳ τὸ κοινὸν σῶμα τῆς Ἐκκλησίας βαστάζοντές τε καὶ
ἐρείδοντες. Ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ τὸν Θεὸν ἀγαπᾷν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας, καὶ τὸν πλησίον ὡς
ἑαυτὸν, ὡς διὰ στύλων μαρμαρίνων, τὸ κοινὸν σῶμα τῆς Ἐκκλησίας βαστάζειν. Ὁ
γὰρ ἐν ταῖς δυσὶ ταύταις τελειωθεὶς ἐντολαῖς, στύλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς Ἐκκλησίας
κατασκευάζεται· ὥστε τοῖς δυσὶ τούτοις κατορθώμασιν, ὅλον τὸ σῶμα τῆς
Ἐκκλησίας, καθάπερ κνήμαις τισὶν ἐπερείδεσθαι, τοῦ χρυσίου θεμελίου τῆς κατὰ
πίστιν βάσεως τὸ ἀκλινὲς καὶ ἀμετάθετον καὶ τὸ ἐν παντὶ ἀγαθῷ πάγιον τοῖς

notes: Source checked clause by clause against PG 69 col. 1289 (Khazarzar transcription).

The row's first clause belongs to the sentence translated in u02-rem-close; the row's last words 'λογισμοῖς ἐμποιοῦντος' sit at the head of u03-rem-early and are translated here so the sentence is whole.
Negation, agency and doctrine checked: Christ is the golden foundation; the apostles and the perfected are the pillars.

The source row opens with 'μαρμαρίνους τεθεμελιωμένους ἐπὶ βάσεις χρυσᾶς', the end of the Song of Songs 5:15 sentence that begins in u02-rem-close; it is translated there, and this row begins with the next sentence.

The last sentence runs across the row break: the source split puts its final words 'λογισμοῖς ἐμποιοῦντος' at the head of u03-rem-early. They are translated here so the sentence is whole; u03-rem-early begins with the next sentence.
'οἳ θεμέλιον τὸν Χριστὸν χρυσὸν λεχθέντα' is elliptical (no verb); rendered 'who have Christ as their foundation, and He is the one here called gold'.

'οὕσπερ εἶπε Παῦλος ἑδραίωμα': Paul calls the Church 'pillar and bulwark of the truth' (1 Timothy 3:15); Cyril applies the word to the apostles themselves. 'Bulwark' is used rather than the older 'ground'.
'καθάπερ κνήμαις τισίν' is rendered 'as if on legs'; λόγος ὑγιαίνων is 'sound speech' (compare Titus 2:8).
